title: Proton pump inhibitors and hospitalization with hypomagnesemia: a population-based case-control study
authors: Zipursky J, Macdonald EM, Hollands S, Gomes T, Mamdani MM, Paterson JM, et al.
followUp: exposure within 365 days before the index date; Ontario databases April 2002 to March 2012
population: Ontario residents aged 66 years or older: 366 hospitalised with hypomagnesaemia and 1464 controls matched on age, sex, kidney disease and diuretic use
funder: This project was supported by research funds from Canadian Drug Safety and Effectiveness Research Network (CDSERN) and by the Institute for Clinical Evaluative Sciences (ICES), which is funded by a grant from the Ontario Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care (MOHLTC). The funders had no role in study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish, or preparation of the manuscript.
authorConflicts: One author (MMM) has been on advisory boards or received honoraria from AstraZeneca, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Eli Lilly, GlaxoSmithKline, Hoffmann-La Roche, Novartis, Novo Nordisk and Pfizer; the others declared none.
result: Current PPI use (within 90 days) was associated with hospitalisation with hypomagnesaemia (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.93); among patients receiving diuretics adjusted OR 1.73 (1.11 to 2.70), among those not receiving diuretics 1.25 (0.81 to 1.91). H2-receptor antagonists were not associated (adjusted OR 1.06, 0.54 to 2.06). The authors estimate one excess hospitalisation with hypomagnesaemia among 76,591 outpatients treated with a PPI for 90 days. Serum magnesium values were unavailable.
